sentences.text: Although the name means "unarmed" because no plates were found in the original bones, scientists now agree this animal was an armored dinosaur.
This creature belonged to the bird-hipped dinosaurs and likely moved on four legs while wearing protective armor.
Adults grew to be about five meters long, stood nearly two meters high, and weighed roughly two and a half tonnes.
Researchers have found only a single fossil record of this dinosaur in major global databases.
Harry Seeley created the genus name in 1879 after finding a partial skeleton at a site in Cambridgeshire.
The initial collection included many bones such as ribs, limb parts, and jaw fragments from the Cambridge Greensand Formation.
Later experts chose a specific right shoulder blade as the official representative specimen for the group.
Pereda-Suberbiola and Barrett (1998) suggested that the lack of armor in the specimen Anoplosaurus curtonotus was due to the animal's young age at death.
Modern taxonomy places this animal in the superfamily Ankylosauria, the family Nodosauridae, and the subfamily Struthiosaurinae.
Studies link it closely to other genera like Silvisaurus and Texasetes.
This dinosaur roamed Europe during the Middle Cretaceous, specifically within the Cenomanian stage between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.

A second species named Anoplosaurus major is now thought to be a mix of an ankylosaur neck and an iguanodont tail, and some researchers believe the fossils might actually come from the Upper Gault Clay rather than the Greensand.
